top_story: After weeks of coercive signaling that began with Trump’s March threat against Iran’s power grid, Washington and Tehran moved on 8 April into a conditional ceasefire that calmed markets and raised prospects of reopening the Strait of Hormuz. That de-escalatory opening was quickly undercut hours later when Israel launched its largest strike of the war against Hezbollah, hitting multiple Lebanese cities and killing at least 254 people while wounding hundreds more. The scale of the attack deepened civilian trauma in Lebanon and gave Tehran grounds to warn it could step back from the overnight ceasefire, linking the Lebanese front directly to Gulf shipping and energy stability. The immediate takeaway is that a narrow US-Iran pause has not contained the wider conflict system, where Israeli military action can rapidly reignite regional escalation and impose the heaviest costs on Lebanese civilians.
